key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches virtual perovskite solar-cell shortlists with recipes near high-performing measured devices.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help prioritize candidate compositions, device layers, and processing recipes before costly fabrication.
method: Generate recipes with reinforcement learning guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support using a reference pool of 890 measured devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised top-ten mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74%; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates reached 23–24% for PPO/RPPO versus 2.9% for random screening and 10% for the strongest baselines.
watch_item: Neighborhood support is similarity-sensitive, and the results do not establish experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
